The control room, drawn by the stylesheet it ships.

Live record. Every shipped specimen is rendered by the app's own stylesheets, inlined byte for byte. The bar (§04) and the usage column (§05) landed on 2026-09-09, the deck (§07) on 2026-09-10 and project colour (§02) on 2026-09-11; §07's specimens are still the record's own drawing of the decided frame, to be swapped for the shipped deck rules. styles/tokens.cssstyles/godview.cssviews/swarm/swarm.cssviews/swarm/agent-bubble.css The switches above flip theme and motion for every specimen. §08 is the real system-control panel, wired.
Four rules, before anything else
  1. Puppeteer is Godview's home. Godview iterates here. It ships as one of vibe-field's four views: Canvas · Godview · History · Assistant. §13 ownership
  2. Godview has its own design system. It inherits from vibe-field's kit at a minimum, a short list of tokens. The instrument skin, its type and its geometry are Godview's own. Part I§01 palette§04 bar§05 usage§07 deck
  3. Project colour governs. vibe-field deals one hue per project. Godview plays well with it: colour is inherited from the project, never chosen locally. §02 project colour
  4. The monitor is an open SDK. Behind one well-designed abstraction, anyone builds their own view of the agents, and design there is open for creativity. Swarm, list and rain are three examples; swarm is the product view. Each owns its own design language, so each has its own section. Part II§09 contract§10 swarm§11 list§12 rain
Part I

The shell: Godview's own system

The bar, the stage frame, the deck and the panel. One palette, one voice, one geometry. Rule 2 lives here.

The instrument palette

State and identity

State: one meaning each
Accents: a session hashed to a slot, until 2026-09-11

FNV-1a over the session id, modulo eight, retired 2026-09-11: the colour is the project's now, dealt, not hashed (§02). An accent grouped and labelled; it never signalled state.

02

Project colour: one dealt hue per project rule 3 · in code 2026-09-11 · revised 2026-09-12

vibe-field's governing system. A colour belongs to a project, dealt once and kept for life. Every agent in that project wears it: as the tag before its name, the flood and the centre light of its body, and the rule and wash of the list and the rain. A pane owns a colour of its own, dealt on a parallel wheel (revised 2026-09-12, below); a session shows the pane's colour as its band and, in the selected pane, as its light. A terminal with no agent belongs to no project and wears no project colour. In this skin nothing changes but what --agent-color holds.

LawWhy
P-1One project, one colour, for life.It does not move when a project is added, deleted or renamed.
P-2Only hue carries identity.Lightness and chroma are the theme's, shared by every project. No project is louder by accident.
P-3Colour is an index, never the identifier.Colour makes finding fast; the name makes it certain. Past two dozen, repeat a hue rather than fake a difference.
P-4Everything in the folder inherits; nothing downstream chooses.An agent wears it because it runs there. A pane does not: a pane's colour is its own, from the pane wheel, and says where a session is, never what it is.

Dealt, not hashed

The 333° wheel, the 27° band around --vf-select withheld, the six state hues marked outside. Large dots: this page's projects, in first-seen order. Small: the next four dealt.

hue(seq) = (258 + seq · φ · 333) mod 333, skipping the band. The golden ratio keeps every prefix spread; hashing a path clusters. Lightness and chroma come from the theme (--tint-l 0.60 light · 0.74 dark, --tint-c 0.15), so a project is the same colour in both.

A project is a canonical source root. Worktrees and copies fold into the repository they were cut from, and a launch in a subfolder folds into it too; the branch tells them apart. A folder becomes a project the first time an agent runs in it. A shell wears the ramp until an agent runs in it: a bare terminal is nobody's, wherever it sits, and so is the pane that shows it.

Inheritance through the agent, drawn with the skin's own parts. The circles wear the hue in their context fill, ignition and link ring; the badges wear it filled on the active pane, outlined elsewhere; a bare shell wears none, even inside the project. The observed mark is unchanged: the link ring now also says which project, because pane and circle share one colour.

Where it lands

SurfaceTakes the project colourStays monochrome
Swarm bodythe band once mounted, the light beyond it only while its pane is the selected one, the flood when blocked, the light at a working body's centrethe body, its size, the gauge, the bars, the figures and every word
List rowthe dot, the left rule when mounted, the border when activeevery word
Rainthe wash behind a mounted columnheads and tails, which follow status
Deckthe badge, the active pane's rim and glowthe terminal, which is Ghosttea's

In code, 2026-09-11

Main owns identity, the renderer owns colour, and a pane owns neither. What landed, and where it bent:

  • A project registry in main (project-registry.ts, projects.json beside the other host preferences): deal(source) → { key, name, seq }. The key is the workspace identity, the real path folded to its Git toplevel, so a worktree, a copy and a subfolder launch all land on the repository. Sequences are never reused, deals are serialized so two agents starting at once in a new folder share one, and a corrupt file costs only the order. A session is dealt as it is registered; an adopted session, which arrives synchronously, is dealt after the fact and re-broadcast.
  • AgentSessionInfo.project carries { key, name, seq } to the renderer. MonitorAgent.color is the project tint (project-tint.ts): the hue dealt from the sequence, the theme's lightness and chroma, converted to sRGB hex in TypeScript with chroma given up until the colour fits the gamut, because the swarm and the rain paint into canvases that cannot ask the engine. A session with no project, a bare terminal or one main has not folded yet, wears the ramp. agentAccentSlot and the accent list in the palette retired.
  • The pane hue walk retired. Pane colours are derived from the agents mounted in them and decoratePane answers only for a pane holding an agent; a neutral pane draws its own line and glow in the ink (deck.css), its selected badge fills in the ink and writes in the ground, and its verbs are the ink. Attachments carry pane ids and no colours, so the swarm's mount light, the list's rule and the rain's wash all take the session's own colour.
  • Two tokens, --tint-l (0.60 light · 0.74 dark) and --tint-c (0.15), on the Godview root per theme until the kit lands them; the palette reads them and the lab deals its fixture projects from them.
  • Later the same day: a mounted body wears the band alone; the light beyond it belongs only to the body whose pane is selected (swarm-renderer.ts sets the glow flag for a linked, active body). A resting pane holding an agent shows its colour once, as a 1px inset outline on the badge (deck.css); the selected pane still fills the badge and lights the line and the glow.
  • Revised 2026-09-12: the pane colour returns. Tried for a day, a pane wearing its agent's colour was confusing to use: two panes on one project could not be told apart, and a pane's colour changed with what it showed. Each pane now owns a colour (pane-colours.ts): dealt in the order panes open, on the pane wheel, hue(seq + ½) on the same walk, so the first pane and the first project never share a hue, and never dealt twice while the window lives. The attachment carries the pane's colour; a mounted body wears it as the band, the selected pane's body as the light too, and the deck's line, glow, badge outline and verbs are the pane's. The project's colour stays the identity mark, as vibe-field asks: a rounded bar the name's height and a quarter as wide, in the project colour, before the project title on every agent body, plus the flood, the centre light, the list's rule and the rain's wash. The neutral pane rules of deck.css retire; every pane is coloured.
  • Open: the wheel withholds only the select band, as drawn above, so project #1 lands at 131°, a green beside --vf-green. Whether the six state hues should be withheld too is a decision for the wheel, not the build.

Type: the instrument voice

One mono stack at small sizes, heavy weights, wide tracking. Hierarchy is size and letter-spacing; the text ramp is three fixed greys. Each sample is the component's real class in a real root.

05

The usage column decided 2026-09-04 · in code 2026-09-09

Each account is its mark inside its rings, one ring per usage window, the tightest figure beneath. The tiles stack in a 46px column down the stage's left edge, sorted by pressure, and scroll when more than four are present. Hover or focus a tile and its popup opens to the right. The column consumes the same usage batch the panel does today; no terminal text is read.

The tile

At three times size: Claude with three rings (5H · 7D · FABLE), Kimi with two, Antigravity rate limited, then the three unmeasured states: sign in (dashed), not exposed (dotted), no limit data (faint).

Ring slotRadiusWindowExamples
inner8.6the short window5H
middle11.8the week7D
outer15anything else the provider reportsFABLE · OPUS · SPARK · CREDIT · BUDGET · PREMIUM

Stroke 2.1, gap 1.1: three rings fit inside 36px around a 9px mark. The same slot means the same kind of window on every account; empty slots are not drawn.

The column at nine

Live: hover a tile, or tab to one. Kimi's popup is pinned so the record shows it. A tile is 44px tall in the column, so four fit a 224px stage; the count beneath says how many more. Rate limited and hot tiles read at the top; the unmeasured states sit at the bottom of the scroll.

The popup

At one and a half times size: an available account, a rate-limited one, and the three unmeasured states, which say what to do instead of showing rows.

06

The window: bar, stage, deck

One flex column. The stage takes its tunable share (35% by default, 170px minimum) and paints the stage colour at the stage opacity through the stage blur, so everything below shows through. Scanlines and vignette sit on top of all of it.

On the stage: the view, the usage column down the left edge, the runtime inspector top right, the notification feed under the bar. The inspector, feed and column are Puppeteer's own, in the same tokens.

The inspector's facts are real-shaped and invented. The deck wears §07's decided panes. Kimi's popup is pinned; hover any tile for its own.

07

The deck decided 2026-09-10 · in code 2026-09-10

Ghosttea owns the terminal; the skin owns what is drawn around it. Decided, after the minimal exploration: the terminal on its theme's own ground, One Half Light beside Ghostty's dark default, with no card, no divider and no brackets. A 1px line in the mounted agent's project colour (§02) and a soft inner glow mark the selected pane, and only that pane rounds its corners; every pane draws them in its own colour (revised 2026-09-12). The name sits in a badge growing out of the top edge; the model and effort are a quiet readout at the top-left; the context share is a thick grey bar along the bottom edge with its figure in the corner; and the verbs, stop with the turn's time, resume, and fullscreen, appear only under the pointer. The terminal's grid keeps to safe areas above and below, so nothing a TUI draws ever meets the frame; the chrome yields in a set order as a pane narrows; and in VibeField the whole deck is a translucent sheet that blurs the canvas beneath it. When a pane is an empty shell, the field that resumes a past session over chips that launch a new agent is unchanged.

Working record: Minimal Pane Frame, with the compositions the pick was made from, the narrow test and the test against the real TUIs.

In code, 2026-09-10. The deck stylesheet draws the ground, the safe areas, the line, the glow and the radius on Ghosttea's own pane element; the badge, the readout, the verbs, the meter and the figure are one frame the shell portals into each pane, and only the pane colour is still asked of Ghosttea; since 2026-09-12 that colour is the pane's own (§02), dealt as panes open, and a resting pane shows it once, as a 1px outline on its badge. What the build settled: the safe areas are padding on the pane, because Ghosttea sizes its grid from the pane's content box with a 2px origin of its own, so the grid lands at 36 · 30 · 32 · 32 without touching Ghostty's window padding, and the sides tighten by a width attribute the frame keeps; the stop verb sends the agent's own interrupt through Ghosttea's automation, since the runtime has no interrupt service; the resume verb shows only while an ended agent's terminal is still in the pane, because an exit ordinarily hands the pane to a shell and takes the run's monitor with it; Ghosttea's settings button moves to the bottom-left band; the verbs leave by a discrete display transition; and the daemon Godview had been staging turned out to be a 0.7.0 prebuild from August that parsed but did not apply the palette and cursor-text keys; the sibling Ghosttea checkout's 0.11.1 source applies both, so the daemon was rebuilt from it and restaged the same day, and the activation check now also honours a daemon's own “recognized, not applied” diagnostics instead of reading them as a shadowing layer. A profile persisted with the retired light preset moves to One Half Light on its own; a chosen theme is left alone. The specimens below are still the record's own drawing of the decided frame. The empty pane's resume-or-launch overlay is not built.

The frame

Three panes drawn as the real TUIs draw themselves: Claude Code just launched in rosetta, selected, with the pointer inside so the verbs are up; Codex just launched in rosetta at rest, scrolling like a plain terminal so its input band stays in view; and Claude Code an hour into a turn in puppeteer at 88%, which is hot, with the auto-compact warning up. Only the selected pane has the line, the glow and the rounded corners; the resting panes meet with no visible edge, and each badge says where one ends.

☼ One Half Light.

States

Rest; selected; selected with the pointer inside; selected with a hot context; exited with the pointer inside, so the square is the green resume; and a remote machine at rest, with its OS mark. They follow the page theme.

The narrow pane

At 330, 260, 200 and 150px with the pointer inside, then at rest. The rules are container queries on the pane, not on the window: the name takes at most half the pane before it yields to an ellipsis and the readout shrinks before the badge; under 300px the readout hides while the pointer is inside so the verbs have its room; under 220px the readout hides, the stop verb keeps only its square, and the side inset tightens to 16px and 14px while the safe areas keep their height.

As a layer in VibeField

The Godview root is a sheet over the canvas: it blurs what is under it by 24px and the deck tints it with the terminal's ground at 82%. Nothing inside a pane has a ground of its own; the frame, the badge, the meter and the scanlines paint on the sheet. The canvas here is a stand-in: a dot grid, a few cards, a picture and a connector.

☼ One Half Light over the light canvas.

◐ The Ghostty default over the dark canvas.

The empty pane

Left: at rest, Claude's chip under the pointer. Right: “fold” typed, the scope on All, this folder's sessions first. Enter resumes; ⌥ and a digit launch new; plain typing reaches the shell and dismisses the overlay. Review, fork and lead are deferred to the composer bar. A shell shows only its badge.

Part II

The monitor: an open SDK

Inside the stage the shell stops. A view is a pure function of what it is handed, and its look is its own. Three ship today; each is a standalone design system below. Rule 4 lives here.

09the view contract10swarm11list12rain
09

The view contract rule 4

A view is one folder plus a line in the registry. It never reaches the runtime, a terminal or the workspace, which is what keeps it unable to read meaning from terminal text.

What a view receives
agentsMonitorAgent[]: id · status idle | working | blocked · project · detail · color · stale? · active · attachment? · agent? (provider, model, branch, contextWindow)
actionsselect(agent) · createAt(position?)
parametersthe numeric bag the view declared, clamped and persisted by the shell
palettethe live tokens, resolved once: accents, status colours, the rain tokens. Passed, because a canvas cannot inherit a custom property
Who owns what
the shell givesthe stage box and its height, the theme class, the CRT overlays, the TUNE panel for the view's own controls, the chrome slot, the inspector, the feed
the view ownseverything painted inside the stage: palette, type, geometry, motion, interaction, tunables
 
export const rainMonitorView: AgentMonitorView = {
  id: 'rain',
  label: 'RAIN',
  parameterGroups: RAIN_PARAMETER_GROUPS,
  Component: RainView,
};

Two constraints, then freedom. Status comes from status, identity from color, never from words on a screen. Stale is presentation, never a fourth state. Beyond that: a pixel RPG, a matrix, a table.

10

Swarm the product view · locked 2026-09-09 · in code

Bodies in a field, drawn on one WebGPU canvas. Status is the body: its colour, its size, its light. Identity is the accent, in three places only. Physics keeps them apart.

Locked on 2026-09-09 after thirty rounds in the swarm lab, where every reading was drawn by the production renderer, shaders and model over fixture agents and the losers were deleted as they lost. The pictures here are captures of that lab (Swarm Lab, pnpm --filter godview swarm-lab); the build is RFC 005 in the Puppeteer repo, apps/godview/src/renderer/views/swarm. Nothing on a body comes from terminal text: status, context, usage, model, effort, the branch and the latest reply are Core's monitor state.

Its palette

Bodies composite at the fill opacity (72%) so they stay glass over the field. The accent is the session's project colour (§02), and it appears in exactly three places: the band of a mounted body, with the light beyond it only while its pane is the selected one, the flood of a blocked body, and the light at a working body's centre. Everything else on a body is the theme's ink and greys.

Glyphs are the OS monospace face rasterised at the device pixel ratio into an atlas and drawn as quads snapped to device pixels. Each line is fitted to the circle's chord at its height and ends in an ellipsis when it must.

The drawn states

StateRadiusBodyMarksLines
Terminal, empty50transparent, 1.5px dashed rim at ink 52%folder markname · empty
Terminal, running50transparent, solid rim at ink 22%, a comet sweeping the rim every 1.4sfolder markname · running · elapsed
Agent, idle50idle fillcontext ring in the ink; when unread, the latest reply led by a blue dotname · model · effort · reply
Agent, working60 – 80working fill, 1px working rim, a resting drop shadow breathing over 3s, an accent light at the centre breathing with the markburn bars in the ink either side of a baseline, context ring in the ink, the agent's mark behind the copy, the context figure top and the total bottombranch · name · model · effort
Agent, blocked50blocked (inverted) fill flooded by the accent from the centre, 95% at the centre and about 44% at the rim; no rimthe latest reply led by an orange dot, or the blocker's kind; the ink is whichever of the theme's stands furthest from the floodname · model · effort · reply

A mounted body, in any state, wears its own colour as a band a thirtieth of the radius wide just outside the rim; the light beyond it is worn by one body only, the one whose pane is the selected pane. The band and the light are the pane's own colour (revised 2026-09-12); the project's colour is the tag before the name. Stale evidence dims a body to 58% and desaturates it. A working body's radius is its share of the working sessions' tokens: the least stays at 60, the most takes 80, the rest fall between in proportion; a lone session, or a tie, is 60.

Anatomy of a working body

☼ The largest working body, 80, at two times size.

◐ The same on the dark theme.

From the top: the context figure on the top chord; the context ring on the rim, a hairline track with the gauge from twelve o'clock; the agent's mark, lifted above the copy's centre, breathing behind it; the branch with its green dot; the project's tag, a rounded bar in the project colour, then the name; model · effort; the burn bars either side of their baseline, the completion side up and the prompt side down; the session's total tokens on the bottom chord. The accent shows once inside the body, as the soft light at its centre.

Physics and tunables

radiusWorkingMax8040 – 160
radiusBlocked5020 – 160

Matter.js, stepped inline on the render loop; the visual radius follows the physics radius on a spring. Drag moves a body; a tap mounts it in the active pane. The renderer is one canvas and one render pass in five pipelines, field · shadow · body · glow · text, every edge an analytic coverage of the distance to the rim.

The field

☼ Eight bodies settled under centre gravity, as the swarm rests: two terminals, an idle and an unread agent, three working at 60, 70 and 80, one of them mounted, and a blocked one.

◐ The same field on the dark theme.

Project colour here

The accent is --agent-color, the project tint (§02); a bare terminal has none and wears the ramp. It appears in three places only: the pane band and light, the blocked flood, and the working body's centre light. The gauge, the bars, the figures, the marks and the type are the theme's ink, so the field reads as grey bodies with coloured lights, not as coloured bodies.

13

Ownership

Tokens move in vibe-field first: DESIGN.md, then the kit, then the vendored copy here. The skin has no such ladder; it carries the same selectors in both apps, so a change lands in one and is copied to the other with its reasons.

Puppeteer · apps/godview/src/renderer
styles/tokens.cssthe kit's tokens, vendored verbatim
styles/godview.cssthe shell: bar, stage, chrome, deck, CRT, panel, inspector, feed, usage; the list and rain rules
views/swarm/*the product view: presentation, physics, two stylesheets, parameters
views/list/*the table and its parameters
views/rain/*the stream, its reconciler, its parameters
monitor/monitor-palette.tstokens resolved for views
AgentIcon.tsxthree marks today; fourteen from rosetta's registry once the build lands
monitor/registry.tsthe line a new view adds
TweakPanel.tsx · main.tsxthe panel; the shell that composes the window
Host differences: mechanics, not design
  • The window is the Godview. No overlay to open; the bar doubles as the drag region.
  • Physics is inline, not in a worker. The circle cannot tell.
  • Core says blocked where vibe-field says waiting.
  • Not ported: mock and remote chips, mesh fault faces, kill, perf readout, terminal-mode switch.
  • Added: the inspector, the feed, the usage column.
Decided since 2026-09-04, and where each stands
  • The glyph bar (§04) replaces the header: one control recipe as a skin class, marks drawn not typed.
  • The usage column and its popup (§05) replace the account-usage panel, in a chrome slot narrowed to 46px.
  • The fourteen marks vendored from rosetta behind the icon component; the three OS marks beside them.
  • The deck (§07), in code 2026-09-10: One Half Light as the light preset, a persisted “Ghosttea Light” profile moving to it on its own; the deck stylesheet replaces the badge, the rim and the divider: the selected pane's line, glow and rounded corners on Ghosttea's pane, the grid inset to the safe areas by the pane's padding, and a frame portalled into each pane for the name badge, the readout, the grey context meter and the pointer's verbs, with container-query rules for narrow panes; stop and resume through two small bridge calls; the OS mark still waits for a platform field the remote protocol does not yet carry, a tether glyph standing in; and, in VibeField, the host lowers the deck's opacity and blurs the root. Still to build: the resume field and agent chips as the empty pane's overlay.
  • Project colour (§02), in code 2026-09-11: a registry in main deals every canonical source root a sequence for life and hands it to the renderer on the session; the theme's tint turns it into the one colour a project wears in the swarm, the list, the rain and the deck; a pane owns a colour of its own from the parallel pane wheel (revised 2026-09-12); a mounted body wears the pane's colour as the band, the selected pane's body alone the light, a resting pane outlines its badge in its colour, and the project's colour is the tag before the name; the session accents retire.
Regenerating this page

Re-inline the four stylesheets into the four <style> blocks at the top, in order; rosetta's marks are the fifth input, the three OS marks the sixth, and One Half Light's sixteen colours from Ghosttea's catalog the seventh. Nothing else is derived.
